idiom_name: hand-written protocol registry plus Foundation Bundle resource lookup
implementation_notes: Swift has no general runtime lookup service: a name-to-service binding is a registry you write - typically a dictionary keyed by an enum or string holding protocol existentials, populated at composition time - so ownership is explicit and a miss is a typed error instead of a stringly runtime surprise. The one built-in lookup service is Foundation's Bundle, which locates resources by name 'without knowing the structure of the bundle': Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) and path(forResource:) search global, region, language and development-language locations and apply device (~iphone) and scale (@2x) modifiers. For class-name lookup there is NSClassFromString, but it goes through the Objective-C runtime and cannot see Swift-only types, so it remains an escape hatch rather than an idiom.
pitfalls: Bundle lookup performs filesystem I/O per call and follows a documented precedence in which global resources shadow localized ones with the same name; the optional result must be handled explicitly.
String-keyed registries lose type safety; prefer enum or type keys and fail fast with a typed error instead of force-unwrapping a lookup result.
A registry built at composition time can go stale if a service is replaced - store factories or re-resolve at defined points instead of caching instances forever.
